topic: The Emily Spectrum: Modes and Eigenvectors
audience: High-school seniors; first-principles teaching, with concrete prerequisite capabilities and taught bridges.
prerequisites: Signed arithmetic, fractions, ratios, powers, linear equations, and coordinate graphs
learning_outcomes: Apply an adjacency matrix to a short node pattern
Derive the path eigenvalues and compare eigenvectors
Recover the seven spectral multiplicities and all 27 modes
Reconstruct a small state from mode coefficients
Test the operator and map behind a proposed spectral identification
requested_deliverables: capstone.md with full answers and rubric
assumptions: A topical short course, not a semester per topic. Pacing is 55-minute core lessons plus capstone periods; split dense lessons if actual learner load requires it.
No prior calculus, abstract algebra, university linear algebra, or quantum mechanics unless explicitly taught earlier.
Required core assessments must be solvable with taught finite examples. Clearly label deeper recognition-only extensions.
Markdown is the delivery format; no PDF or Word generation is required.

course_map.assessment_target: Apply an adjacency matrix to a short node pattern

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Write adjacency as neighbor sums with node order(-1,0,1). Distinguish it from incidence D and graph Laplacian. Use A=[[0,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,0]] for the open three-node path.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For f=(1,2,3), Af=(2,4,2); each component sums adjacent node values. A(1,1,1)=(1,2,1), so a constant pattern is not preserved up to one common multiplier.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For f=(2,-1,0), Af=(-1,2,-1). For f=(1,0,0), Af=(0,1,0). Preserve negative entries and node order.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A maps3 node values to3 node values; D maps edge values to node divergence. Their shapes and definitions differ, even when a small example obscures the distinction.

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define Av=lambda v component by component, require v nonzero, and teach square root as positive number with specified square. Work a two-node swap before the path; scaling eigenvectors does not change their eigenvalue.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For A2=[[0,1],[1,0]], (1,1) has eigenvalue1 and(1,-1) eigenvalue-1. Multiplying either pattern by3 preserves its eigenvalue; zero vector is excluded because it would satisfy every scalar equation.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Verify A2(2,2)=(2,2) and A2(2,-2)=-(2,-2). On P3 verify A(2,0,-2)=0, a nonzero zero-eigenvalue pattern.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: For P3, (1,1,1) is not an eigenvector because(1,2,1) is not a scalar multiple. The eigenvalue0 means zero output on that pattern, not a forbidden zero input.

course_map.title: The three-node path spectrum
course_map.worked_example_capability: Derive the path eigenvalues and compare eigenvectors
course_map.assessment_target: Derive the path eigenvalues and compare eigenvectors

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Retain EA-12-E06-1 including C12-EIG-EX1/P1/D1. Derive the three path modes from endpoint equations: lambda=0 gives center0/opposite endpoints; lambda nonzero gives equal endpoints and lambda^2=2. Normalize using actual squared lengths and verify all pairwise dot products.

worked_example.task_and_answer: C12-EIG-EX1: v+=(1,sqrt2,1),v0=(1,0,-1),v-=(1,-sqrt2,1), eigenvalues sqrt2,0,-sqrt2. Norms2,sqrt2,2; u+=v+/2,u0=v0/sqrt2,u-=v-/2. Each row multiplication verifies the pair and all mutual dots vanish.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: C12-EIG-P1 verifies A(2,0,-2)=0. Also normalize(2,2sqrt2,2) by4, recover u+, and independently check A u-= -sqrt2 u-. Compute u+ dot u-= (1-2+1)/4=0 and u0 dot u-=0.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: C12-EIG-D1 rejects(1,1,1). Verify sqrt2*sqrt2=2 rather than replacing it by a rounded decimal. All normalized modes have norm1; a general spectral theorem is not an untaught assessed proof.

teaching_anchor.original_assessment_target: Derive the path eigenvalues and compare eigenvectors

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define product pattern v(i,j,k)=a(i)b(j)c(k) and open product adjacency as the sum of three neighbor actions, not a product of matrices. Derive eigenvalue addition by distributing the finite sums.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Two path factors u+ and u0 give eigenvalue sqrt2+0=sqrt2. Three factors u+,u+,u- give sqrt2. At node(0,0,0), center components yield value -sqrt2/4, neighbor sum -1/2, equal to sqrt2 times the value.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Factors u+,u0,u- give eigenvalue0. Factors u-,u-,u0 give-2sqrt2. For the latter check node(-1,-1,-1): value=1/(4sqrt2), neighbor sum=-1/2, agreeing with eigenvalue times value. Product norm equals product of norms=1.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Multiplying eigenvalues would give0 for u+,u0,u- but would also incorrectly give0 for u+,u0,u0, whose correct sum is sqrt2. Pin open adjacency and coordinate order before using the product rule.

course_map.title: Counting Emily multiplicities
course_map.worked_example_capability: Recover the seven spectral multiplicities and all 27 modes
course_map.assessment_target: Recover the seven spectral multiplicities and all 27 modes

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Count ordered mode triples, distinguish sign of eigenvalue from antipodal function parity and node chi. Introduce reflection Rf(L)=f(-L); even and odd parts (f+Rf)/2 and(f-Rf)/2. Count fixed center and13 pairs explicitly.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Adding coefficients in{-1,0,1} three times gives multiplicities1,3,6,7,6,3,1 for m=-3..3. For m=0: one(0,0,0) plus six permutations of(-1,0,1)=7. Antipodal functions have14 even coordinates and13 odd; node chi=(-1)^sumL instead has13 positive nodes,14 negative.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For m=1: three permutations of(1,0,0) plus three of(1,1,-1)=6. Sum all seven multiplicities=27. On P3 state(1,2,3), even=(2,2,2), odd=(-1,0,1); each pair decodes as even plus/minus odd, center stays even. Independently count the27-node window as13 swapped pairs plus one fixed center: even14,odd13. Sum even-lambda populations3+7+3=13 positive-chi nodes and odd-lambda populations1+6+6+1=14 negative-chi nodes; these count node labels, not function parity.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Seven lambda-sheet populations have the same list of counts but classify nodes; Emily multiplicities classify adjacency modes. Thirteen antipodal pairs,13 decoder channels and seven syndrome dimensions are separately typed objects, not proved identical by counting.

teaching_anchor.explicit_multiplicity_bridge: First multiply two factor lists to obtain counts[1,2,3,2,1] for m=-2..2; convolve with[1,1,1] to get[1,3,6,7,6,3,1]. Students enumerate small triples; no general generating-function theorem required.

course_map.title: Reading a state through modes
course_map.worked_example_capability: Reconstruct a small state from mode coefficients
course_map.assessment_target: Reconstruct a small state from mode coefficients

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach coefficient c_j=u_j dot f and reconstruction f=sum c_j u_j using the established orthonormal basis. Separately teach retained uniform mean and antipodal parts. Removing a uniform coordinate is not deleting an Emily eigenmode.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For f=(1,2,3), coefficients in order(+,0,-) are(2+sqrt2,-sqrt2,2-sqrt2); reconstruct f exactly with residual(0,0,0). Mean2 and centered part(-1,0,1) also reconstruct f; this is a different coordinate representation.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For f=(2,0,0), coefficients(1,sqrt2,1) rebuild f. Even=(1,0,1), odd=(1,0,-1); mean2/3 and centered part(4/3,-2/3,-2/3) rebuild it. Retain all coefficients, mean and signed components used in the chosen representation. On the Lucas graph, count one neighbor per noncentral coordinate and two per central coordinate: corner3,edge-center4,face-center5,center6. Therefore A1 is not a scalar multiple of1. This explicitly tests the uniform-mode claim before capstone use.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: For Lucas functions, removing retained uniform mean leaves13 even+13 odd centered coordinates. But A1 is the degree vector, with8 entries3,12 entries4,6 entries5,1 entry6. Constant line is not invariant: no quotient adjacency operator or26-mode Emily spectrum follows. Any projected operator requires a separate definition and verification.

course_map.title: Spectral resemblance and typed identity
course_map.worked_example_capability: Test the operator and map behind a proposed spectral identification
course_map.assessment_target: Test the operator and map behind a proposed spectral identification

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define a proposed identification using domain, codomain, operators and an explicit invertible coordinate map T; test B T=T A. Teach a2x2 example before any source carrier comparison. Preserve source-reported statuses and unresolved maps.

worked_example.task_and_answer: A=diag(1,2), T=[[0,1],[1,0]], B=diag(2,1): BT=TA=[[0,2],[1,0]], so T is an actual relabeling of the operator. T(3,4)=(4,3), T again recovers(3,4).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For the same A,B, proposed T=I fails: B-A=diag(1,-1). They have equal eigenvalue counts but this particular map is not an intertwiner. For T=swap, state(1,-2) maps(-2,1) and recovers exactly.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Count matches among Emily modes, sheet populations, antipodal pairs, decoder channels and syndrome coordinates do not provide T or an operator. R commutes with open adjacency, so even/odd function sectors are invariant; removing constants additionally is not justified by that fact. No projected operator is introduced in this core.

course10.typed_Devon_object: The typed reduced object containing direct metric, cofactors, reciprocal metric, common scale, A2 shape fiber, scalar lift, branch modes, and their invertible maps; its components are not collapsed into one untyped vector.
course10.area_tangent_to_scalar: dln Gamma2=9dln A_ab+8dln A_ac-11dln A_bc from explicitly named M19 branch; it yields row(17,-2,-3) under fixed-angle edge scaling. This does not certify other M19 branches or assert dynamics.
course10.scope_guard: SA-10 replaces dimensional log shorthand by ln(A/A0). All logs use positive quantities. Two shape coordinates describe three area ratios modulo common scale; arbitrary edge-angle shear requires further coordinates. J is a tangent map; finite exact classroom maps are separately declared.

course11.coordinate_choice: Open vertices lexicographic in{0,1,2}^3. Open edges oriented increasing coordinate, axes0,1,2 then lexicographic tails. Root0; parent decrements first nonzero coordinate. Each non-tree edge is a chord, cycle=+1 on that chord plus signed tree path head-to-tail. Wrap edges point2->0; ordered by axis and lexicographic tail. Wrap winding W_axis=sum9 chord coefficients; mean=W/9; first8 zero-sum details free, ninth=-sum8. Circulation reconstructed by fundamental-cycle sum; a general flow additionally retains its tree remainder.
course11.integer_guard: This is a real/rational coordinate decomposition. For integer coefficients, mean/detail coordinates obey compatibility constraints; no unsupported integral direct-product claim.
course11.dynamics_guard: The52=28+24 and55=52+3 counts are finite coordinate counts; no F4 action, force, memory lifetime or dynamics is derived.

course12.operator: Open unweighted Cartesian-product adjacency on lexicographic triples; P3 node order(-1,0,1). Orthonormal modes ordered(+,0,-).
course12.source_amendment_preservation: Retain SA-12 and EA-12-E06-1 verbatim including legacy exercise IDs. Function parity14even/13odd becomes13+13 centered coordinate count only with retained mean. Node chi13+/14-,13 antipodal pairs,13 decoder channels,7 syndrome dimensions,7 sheet populations and7 distinct Emily eigenvalues remain different objects. M17 channel matrix is independently checked as13x6 rank6, but its full decoder is recognition-only in this course.
course12.uniform_guard: A1=degree vector is not constant. The constant line is not adjacency invariant; quotienting constants does not induce open adjacency, nor delete one Emily eigenmode. If a builder adds a projected operator, it must explicitly define Q A Q on im Q and check its own spectrum; it cannot inherit the Emily list. The recommended core introduces no projected operator.
course12.identity_guard: Every spectral identity names both operators and map and verifies B T=T A. Count agreement alone is insufficient.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For f=(1,2,3), Af=(2,4,2); each component sums adjacent node values. A(1,1,1)=(1,2,1), so a constant pattern is not preserved up to one common multiplier.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For f=(2,-1,0), Af=(-1,2,-1). For f=(1,0,0), Af=(0,1,0). Preserve negative entries and node order.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A maps3 node values to3 node values; D maps edge values to node divergence. Their shapes and definitions differ, even when a small example obscures the distinction.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Define Av=lambda v component by component, require v nonzero, and teach square root as positive number with specified square. Work a two-node swap before the path; scaling eigenvectors does not change their eigenvalue.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For A2=[[0,1],[1,0]], (1,1) has eigenvalue1 and(1,-1) eigenvalue-1. Multiplying either pattern by3 preserves its eigenvalue; zero vector is excluded because it would satisfy every scalar equation.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Verify A2(2,2)=(2,2) and A2(2,-2)=-(2,-2). On P3 verify A(2,0,-2)=0, a nonzero zero-eigenvalue pattern.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: For P3, (1,1,1) is not an eigenvector because(1,2,1) is not a scalar multiple. The eigenvalue0 means zero output on that pattern, not a forbidden zero input.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Retain EA-12-E06-1 including C12-EIG-EX1/P1/D1. Derive the three path modes from endpoint equations: lambda=0 gives center0/opposite endpoints; lambda nonzero gives equal endpoints and lambda^2=2. Normalize using actual squared lengths and verify all pairwise dot products.

worked_example.task_and_answer: C12-EIG-EX1: v+=(1,sqrt2,1),v0=(1,0,-1),v-=(1,-sqrt2,1), eigenvalues sqrt2,0,-sqrt2. Norms2,sqrt2,2; u+=v+/2,u0=v0/sqrt2,u-=v-/2. Each row multiplication verifies the pair and all mutual dots vanish.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: C12-EIG-P1 verifies A(2,0,-2)=0. Also normalize(2,2sqrt2,2) by4, recover u+, and independently check A u-= -sqrt2 u-. Compute u+ dot u-= (1-2+1)/4=0 and u0 dot u-=0.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: C12-EIG-D1 rejects(1,1,1). Verify sqrt2*sqrt2=2 rather than replacing it by a rounded decimal. All normalized modes have norm1; a general spectral theorem is not an untaught assessed proof.

lessons.original_assessment_target: Derive the path eigenvalues and compare eigenvectors

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Define product pattern v(i,j,k)=a(i)b(j)c(k) and open product adjacency as the sum of three neighbor actions, not a product of matrices. Derive eigenvalue addition by distributing the finite sums.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Two path factors u+ and u0 give eigenvalue sqrt2+0=sqrt2. Three factors u+,u+,u- give sqrt2. At node(0,0,0), center components yield value -sqrt2/4, neighbor sum -1/2, equal to sqrt2 times the value.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Factors u+,u0,u- give eigenvalue0. Factors u-,u-,u0 give-2sqrt2. For the latter check node(-1,-1,-1): value=1/(4sqrt2), neighbor sum=-1/2, agreeing with eigenvalue times value. Product norm equals product of norms=1.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Multiplying eigenvalues would give0 for u+,u0,u- but would also incorrectly give0 for u+,u0,u0, whose correct sum is sqrt2. Pin open adjacency and coordinate order before using the product rule.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Count ordered mode triples, distinguish sign of eigenvalue from antipodal function parity and node chi. Introduce reflection Rf(L)=f(-L); even and odd parts (f+Rf)/2 and(f-Rf)/2. Count fixed center and13 pairs explicitly.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Adding coefficients in{-1,0,1} three times gives multiplicities1,3,6,7,6,3,1 for m=-3..3. For m=0: one(0,0,0) plus six permutations of(-1,0,1)=7. Antipodal functions have14 even coordinates and13 odd; node chi=(-1)^sumL instead has13 positive nodes,14 negative.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For m=1: three permutations of(1,0,0) plus three of(1,1,-1)=6. Sum all seven multiplicities=27. On P3 state(1,2,3), even=(2,2,2), odd=(-1,0,1); each pair decodes as even plus/minus odd, center stays even. Independently count the27-node window as13 swapped pairs plus one fixed center: even14,odd13. Sum even-lambda populations3+7+3=13 positive-chi nodes and odd-lambda populations1+6+6+1=14 negative-chi nodes; these count node labels, not function parity.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Seven lambda-sheet populations have the same list of counts but classify nodes; Emily multiplicities classify adjacency modes. Thirteen antipodal pairs,13 decoder channels and seven syndrome dimensions are separately typed objects, not proved identical by counting.

lessons.explicit_multiplicity_bridge: First multiply two factor lists to obtain counts[1,2,3,2,1] for m=-2..2; convolve with[1,1,1] to get[1,3,6,7,6,3,1]. Students enumerate small triples; no general generating-function theorem required.
lessons.original_assessment_target: Recover the seven spectral multiplicities and all 27 modes

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Teach coefficient c_j=u_j dot f and reconstruction f=sum c_j u_j using the established orthonormal basis. Separately teach retained uniform mean and antipodal parts. Removing a uniform coordinate is not deleting an Emily eigenmode.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For f=(1,2,3), coefficients in order(+,0,-) are(2+sqrt2,-sqrt2,2-sqrt2); reconstruct f exactly with residual(0,0,0). Mean2 and centered part(-1,0,1) also reconstruct f; this is a different coordinate representation.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For f=(2,0,0), coefficients(1,sqrt2,1) rebuild f. Even=(1,0,1), odd=(1,0,-1); mean2/3 and centered part(4/3,-2/3,-2/3) rebuild it. Retain all coefficients, mean and signed components used in the chosen representation. On the Lucas graph, count one neighbor per noncentral coordinate and two per central coordinate: corner3,edge-center4,face-center5,center6. Therefore A1 is not a scalar multiple of1. This explicitly tests the uniform-mode claim before capstone use.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: For Lucas functions, removing retained uniform mean leaves13 even+13 odd centered coordinates. But A1 is the degree vector, with8 entries3,12 entries4,6 entries5,1 entry6. Constant line is not invariant: no quotient adjacency operator or26-mode Emily spectrum follows. Any projected operator requires a separate definition and verification.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Define a proposed identification using domain, codomain, operators and an explicit invertible coordinate map T; test B T=T A. Teach a2x2 example before any source carrier comparison. Preserve source-reported statuses and unresolved maps.

worked_example.task_and_answer: A=diag(1,2), T=[[0,1],[1,0]], B=diag(2,1): BT=TA=[[0,2],[1,0]], so T is an actual relabeling of the operator. T(3,4)=(4,3), T again recovers(3,4).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For the same A,B, proposed T=I fails: B-A=diag(1,-1). They have equal eigenvalue counts but this particular map is not an intertwiner. For T=swap, state(1,-2) maps(-2,1) and recovers exactly.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Count matches among Emily modes, sheet populations, antipodal pairs, decoder channels and syndrome coordinates do not provide T or an operator. R commutes with open adjacency, so even/odd function sectors are invariant; removing constants additionally is not justified by that fact. No projected operator is introduced in this core.

capstone_backward_map.operation: Apply the explicit open P3 adjacency to(2,-1,0) in declared node order.
Verify the two-node eigenpairs and scaled P3 zero mode; exclude the zero vector from the eigenvector definition.
Derive/verify all three exact P3 eigenpairs; normalize, check pairwise orthogonality and reject the constant-path candidate.
Build a product mode from u-,u-,u0, add eigenvalues and verify one component and its neighbor sum.
Enumerate the seven Emily multiplicities; separately derive14-even/13-odd function coordinates,13+/14- node chi and lambda-sheet populations without identifying their carriers.
Reconstruct f=(2,0,0) from all three mode coefficients; separately preserve parity parts, mean and centered detail. Explain13+13 coordinate count and test A1 against a constant multiple.
Check the supplied2x2 swap intertwiner and reject the identity map; identify the missing operator/map in a proposed sheet-to-mode identification.

course_amendment.core_boundary: Finite hand-checkable algebra, small graph calculations and supplied source cards. No general calculus/spectral theorem, arbitrary shear reconstruction, physical force derivation, dynamics inference from counts or exceptional-group identification is silently assessed.
course_amendment.prerequisite_status: Blueprint closure checked for every explicit capstone operation; actual produced lessons/practice still require independent acceptance.
